idiom_name: gateway class over the SQLite/PostgreSQL C APIs, or over SOCI as the driver wrapper
implementation_notes: The C++ standard library has no SQL support, so the gateway is a class per table - the classic structure typed out by hand - sitting either on the raw C APIs (sqlite3_prepare_v2/sqlite3_bind_*, libpq PQexecParams) or on a driver wrapper such as SOCI, whose session << "select name from users where id = :id", use(id), into(name) binds parameters and fills plain values or a soci::rowset<>. Rows stay records: structs, tuples or soci::row instances that the caller reads by column. The hand-rolled form is justified when bind-level control (blobs, streaming, statement caching, zero dependencies) matters; SOCI/OTL pay off when the same code must run over several backends.
pitfalls: A gateway that owns the connection cannot be enlisted in a caller-managed transaction; take the handle by reference and let RAII own statements, not the connection.
Text and blob columns: sqlite3_column_text returns a pointer valid only until the next step - copy into std::string (or the chosen record type) before continuing.
Sharing one connection object across threads without the serialized threading mode corrupts data; C++ gives no synchronization here.
Exposing vector<UserRow> by value for large result sets copies every row; return the reader/rowset range or let the caller pass an output container.
